chapter.title: Thermodynamics
chapter.scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT Physics, Mathematics and Research Reasoning lessons. Models and calculations use stated assumptions. Independent scientific review is pending; this is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Temperature describes thermal equilibrium and relates to microscopic energy distributions. Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference, not a substance stored inside an object.
The zeroth law makes thermal equilibrium transitive: if A and B are separately in thermal equilibrium with C, A and B are in equilibrium with each other.
Equal temperature does not require equal total internal energy. Amount of material, composition and phase can change internal energy at the same temperature.
Use kelvin for absolute-temperature ratios. Celsius intervals equal kelvin intervals, but Celsius zero is not absolute zero.

steps.text: A thermodynamic system is the part selected for study; everything else is surroundings. The boundary determines which exchanges must be counted.
An open system exchanges matter and energy; a closed system exchanges energy but not matter. An isolated system exchanges neither with its surroundings.
A closed system is not automatically adiabatic. Adiabatic means no heat transfer across the boundary, but work can still change internal energy.
State functions depend on state rather than process path. Heat and work depend on the path taken between states, so they are not stored state functions.

steps.text: Use the convention ΔU = Q - Wby, where Q is positive for heat entering the system and Wby is positive for work done by the system on its surroundings.
A gas expanding against external pressure does positive work in this convention. Compression does negative work by the gas, which tends to increase its internal energy.
For a quasistatic pressure-volume process, work by the gas is the area under its P–V curve. A cyclic process returns to its initial internal energy but can exchange net heat and work.
For a monatomic ideal gas with fixed amount, internal energy depends on absolute temperature. During an ideal-gas isothermal process, ΔU = 0; heat and work need not vanish.

lessons.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics and Entropy

steps.text: Entropy is a state function related to energy dispersal and accessible microscopic arrangements. A local entropy decrease can occur when it is offset by a larger surroundings increase.
For a reversible heat transfer at fixed absolute temperature, ΔS = Qrev/T. This expression uses a reversible path, even when the actual process is irreversible.
For an isolated system, total entropy does not decrease. For a spontaneous irreversible process, entropy of the system plus surroundings increases; a reversible idealization has zero total change.
Heat naturally flows from hotter to colder regions without external work. A refrigerator can move heat the other way by requiring work and increasing total entropy.
